body: @cjvolzka Does that mean, that we need 1.16.2?

> @cjvolzka Does that mean, that we need 1.16.2?

I don't know how you evaluated this vulnerability, but currently this issue is similar to CVE-2024-5187. Although the exploitability of this vulnerability is low, it is not ruled out that users may download other models for testing. As for how to modify it, it depends on you.

@gramalingam See the discussion above, would you know of someone with the suitable expertise be able to find a fix to this?

Thanks

> [CVE-2024-5187](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6rq9-53c3-f7vj)



> @gramalingam See the discussion above, would you know of someone with the suitable expertise be able to find a fix to this?
> 
> Thanks

I think the same fix as CVE-2024-5187 is enough. This is what I found when I was doing variant analysis. You can refer to the following link for the specific fix patch: https://github.com/onnx/onnx/commit/3fc3845edb048df559aa2a839e39e95503a0ee34.

I guess @Arashimu is referring to the function in file `onnx/backend/test/Runner/__init__.py` ? Seems to me that we should apply the same patch as the one made elsewhere by https://github.com/onnx/onnx/pull/6145 ?

> I guess @Arashimu is referring to the function in file `onnx/backend/test/Runner/__init__.py` ? Seems to me that we should apply the same patch as the one made elsewhere by #6145 ?

I think so

> @cjvolzka Does that mean, that we need 1.16.2?

Depends on when the fix becomes ready vs when the next release is scheduled. If we decide we want a 1.16.2, I can create a 1.16.2 branch from 1.16.1 and cherrypick the fix.
